title: Stroke-sculpt tool in the mesh viewer with undo/redo history (EditHistory), save to DSL + pass SVGs
description:
Stroke sculpting today is a DSL node plus the stroke-lift route: no Tool, no undo history. Undo means editing or deleting a pass's SVG and re-running. Make it a Tool in the mesh viewer, like the ring and region tools, so a person (or an agent through ixdar-cli control/key) sculpts interactively with undo/redo.

- StrokeSculptTool extends Tool. Its state is the pass list (each pass's SVG text plus its node options: strength, symmetry). Each applied stroke or pass is pushed onto an EditHistory<state>, so undo/redo restore the pass list and the mesh re-evaluates from the sphere through the stroke_sculpt node chain (MESH-70).
- Controls are rows the CLI lists (`ixdar-cli tools`): draw a stroke on the current view (silhouette / ridge / valley / fill, with width and strength), commit pass, undo, redo, toggle symmetry. The undo/redo names show in ui-state like the ring tool's.
- Save writes the DSL and the pass SVGs, the way the ring scene's save writes spline_ring statements. Loading a stroke-sculpt DSL restores the pass list as the tool's state.
- Drawing in the live viewer records the camera with the stroke, as multiview does for SVGs, so a saved pass replays through the same camera.
definition-of-done:
1. The mesh viewer has a stroke-sculpt tool listed by `ixdar-cli tools`, with controls to draw each stroke kind, commit a pass, undo, redo and toggle symmetry.
2. Undo and redo step through applied strokes and passes via EditHistory; ui-state reports the next undo/redo names; after undo the mesh equals the DSL evaluated without that pass.
3. Save writes the DSL and pass SVGs; reopening restores the tool's pass list and gives the same mesh.
4. No new class in the change has a single user.
5. A launch.json entry and screenshots under tmp/ show a stroke drawn, undone and redone.
testing-plan:
1. Draw two strokes through `ixdar-cli control`/`key`, undo one, check the mesh and ui-state; redo, check again.
2. Commit two passes, save, reopen with `model --path`, compare mesh fingerprints.
3. Toggle symmetry, draw one stroke, check the mirror distance.
changes-made: StrokeSculptTool (ixdar/tools/sculpt): the mesh viewer's ctrl+K tool; drag draws a stroke (ctrl+drag orbits, shift+drag pans), 1-4 pick silhouette/ridge/valley/fill, -/= strength, ,/. width, Enter commits the pass, X toggles x symmetry, ctrl+Z undo, ctrl+shift+Z and ctrl+Y redo through EditHistory<List<SculptPass>>, ctrl+S writes the .dsl and pass SVGs; the passes are re-read when a model loads

SculptPass: one stroke_sculpt pass (id, upstream, svg path and text, symmetry, open), the tool's Item in ui-state and the unit its undo snapshots share; withStroke adds a live stroke, statement() writes its DSL line

StrokeSketch: parse(text) split from read(path); a data-views entry may carry a full camera (azimuth elevation distance roll fov centre) that lift uses per cell; addStroke records a live view as a new cell; toSvg serialises the sketch
StrokeSculptNode: the svg port also takes the SVG text itself (a value starting with <), which the tool sets for unsaved passes so they evaluate as their saved files will; NODE_ID constant
MeshNodeViewerScene: hosts the tool; showGraph(source, overrides) runs a tool-built graph without reframing the camera; executeViewerGraph takes extra overrides
StrokeSculptTest.liveStrokesLiftThroughTheViewsTheyWereDrawnOn: two live strokes (rolled, other fov and distance) round-trip toSvg/parse and lift onto their pixel rays

Verified on a copy of stroke_sculpt_head.dsl: ridge then valley stroke, ctrl+Z returns the one-stroke fingerprint (nextUndo 'ridge stroke on pass4', nextRedo 'valley stroke on pass4'), redo returns the two-stroke one, undoing both returns the DSL without pass4; two committed passes saved and reopened with model --path at the same fingerprint (accc3edd) and the same 5 passes; mirror Hausdorff 0.2005 with symmetry off vs 2.5e-7 on; screenshots tmp/mesh71-1..7-*.png; teavm-build OK
review-summary: The mesh viewer gains a stroke-sculpt tool (ctrl+K) that draws strokes on the live view into chained stroke_sculpt passes, with undo and redo through EditHistory and a save to the .dsl plus one SVG per pass. Sculpting no longer means hand-editing pass SVGs and re-running the graph.
